answer: Resist sybils by proving each agent controls a distinct network endpoint: at registration, scattered verifiers triangulate the agent's location from latency measurements, like cargo checked at a wharf before it unloads. Clones on one operator's machines all answer from the same network neighborhood, so their claims spiral into a single point instead of spreading across the map, and only one identity per endpoint earns weight. Renting thousands of servers across networks costs real money per clone, while an honest agent proves its endpoint once and climbs toward the summit of trusted work.
